title: Can the World Cup Help the U.S. Beer Industry Kick Its Slump?
partialText: Bars and stores are uncertain if the soccer tournament will boost beer sales. Still, the maker of Budweiser and Michelob Ultra is going all in.

title: What Is Airbnb For, Exactly?
partialText: The home-sharing app recently added car rentals, groceries and — perhaps most surprisingly — hotels. Brian Chesky, the co-founder and chief executive, is always thinking about how to redesign it.

title: Is This the Future of Air Travel?
partialText: A new all-electric aircraft made a test flight in New York City. Our transportation reporter Niraj Chokshi describes what to know.

title: Joby Demonstrated its Air Taxi in Manhattan, but You Can’t Fly in It Yet
partialText: Aviation start-ups and the Trump administration want to replace helicopters with electric aircraft, but the new vehicles still have to pass arduous tests before the public can use them.

title: Dang Van Phuoc Dies at 90; Intrepid Photojournalist in Vietnam War
partialText: A photographer for The Associated Press, he spent a decade on the front lines of combat in his native Vietnam and lost his right eye in a grenade explosion.

title: When War Breaks Out Over the Family Business, They Get the Call
partialText: As baby boomers begin passing down trillions in assets, advisers who specialize in navigating the process — and the emotions around it — have never been busier.

title: How Your Friend Group Influences How You Spend and Save
partialText: Our spending habits are often influenced by our social circles. You can help shape what it looks like.

title: Making Motherhood and a Long Tennis Career Possible
partialText: Tennis is a solitary sport, but with new fertility benefits, a sisterhood of egg freezers is emerging in locker rooms and players’ lounges.

title: China’s Rise in Drug Development Looms Over U.S.
partialText: Clinical trials in China are getting attention at an international oncology gathering in Chicago. China’s surging biotechnology industry is fueling alarm that U.S. dominance in the field is waning.

title: S.E.C. Proposes to Kill Climate Change Disclosure Rule
partialText: The regulation would have required all publicly traded companies to disclose whether they faced significant risks from climate change and its effects.

title: For Wall Street, the Only Thing Worse Than SpaceX Flopping Is Missing Out
partialText: Elon Musk and his bankers are working to create a self-fulfilling prophecy for the massive public offering: Make investors feel that the risks of passing it up outweigh those of buying into it.

title: Sky-High I.P.O. Pricing Isn’t Great for Real People
partialText: When newly public companies have been valued as richly as SpaceX, OpenAI and Anthropic seem likely to be, the outlook for ordinary investors has been poor.

title: Inside the Room Where War Insurance Is Bought and Sold
partialText: Many of the ships stranded in the Persian Gulf depend on coverage negotiated at Lloyd’s, the center of marine insurance for more than 300 years.

title: Trump Clears Way for Companies to Avoid Taxes in Havens Including Malta and Cyprus
partialText: U.S. companies skirted at least $40 billion in taxes since the beginning of 2025 thanks to schemes in places like Malta, Bermuda and Cyprus.

title: The $900 Billion Giant: How Anthropic Got So Big, So Fast
partialText: The artificial intelligence giant was just valued at $900 billion, surpassing OpenAI. Here are the numbers behind its rise — and headwinds it faces.

title: Luka Doncic on Trying to Bring an N.B.A. Team to Rome
partialText: The superstar is part of group that has bought a basketball team in Italy, with a plan to move the club to Rome in hopes of making it part of a new league.

title: Providence Isn’t an Official World Cup Host but It Sure Is Acting Like One
partialText: A stadium outside Boston that will host seven World Cup games is actually closer to Providence, R.I., prompting officials there to capitalize on that proximity to lure fans.

title: A.I. Doesn’t Have to Mean Layoffs
partialText: A French multinational, Schneider Electric, decided to use artificial intelligence in manufacturing to make workers more productive, rather than to replace them. Here’s how that’s going.

title: ‘Backrooms’ Is Part of a Boomlet in Movies From YouTube Creators
partialText: “Backrooms,” a psychological horror flick opening this weekend, is part of a wave of breakout films from fledgling directors who honed their instincts on YouTube.

title: How NextEra Energy Wielded Political Power in Florida
partialText: NextEra, which is seeking to buy Dominion Energy, has often butted heads with consumer groups, residents and journalists in its home state.

title: How to Travel if You Have Panic Attacks
partialText: You don’t have to let severe anxiety keep you from exploring the world. Here’s how to manage your panic on vacation.

title: Oil Prices Fall as U.S. and Iran Edge Closer to Agreement
partialText: Oil prices and stock markets fluctuated as investors assessed tentative signs of a pact to extend a cease-fire.

title: Europe Is Edging Closer to a Trade War With China. Here’s Why.
partialText: As cheap goods pour in, threatening the continent’s manufacturing sector, a search for solutions is becoming increasingly urgent.

title: ABC Accuses Trump Administration of Threatening Its Broadcast Licenses
partialText: The TV network slammed the Federal Communications Commission, saying the regulator was targeting its station licenses in a campaign of “unconstitutional retaliation.”

title: Treasury Prepares to Make Trump the Face of a New $250 Bill
partialText: Treasury Secretary Bessent backed the idea, which would require legislation allowing a living person to appear on currency.

title: Two Papers Named ‘Star’ Will Duel in D.C. to Win Readers From The Washington Post
partialText: First, The Star was born. Now, The Washington Star is reborn. Both are hoping to win readers ceded by recent layoffs at The Washington Post.

title: Watchdog Agency Seeks to Reverse Its Win Against Firm Run by Winklevoss Twins
partialText: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission filed jointly with a company run by the Winklevoss twins to overturn their settlement.

title: Everlane Co-Founder, Shocked by Shein Acquisition, Wants a Redo
partialText: Michael Preysman, who ran the brand for a decade, can’t believe what happened to the company he built. Can he start over?

title: Trump Refiles $10 Billion Lawsuit Against The Wall Street Journal
partialText: An earlier version of the defamation suit, which focused on an article about a birthday note to Jeffrey Epstein, was dismissed by a judge.

title: Bari Weiss Names Nick Bilton to Lead CBS’s ‘60 Minutes’ in Major Shake-Up
partialText: Bari Weiss, CBS’s editor in chief, named Nick Bilton, a tech journalist and filmmaker, as the show’s executive producer. The network also fired two on-air correspondents.

title: Fired BP Chair Manifold Rejects ‘Lies’ About His Ouster
partialText: Albert Manifold, who was abruptly dismissed by the oil company this week, hit back in a new statement that admitted he “pushed hard” but never crossed a line.

title: Iran War Lifts a Second Inflation Reading to Highest Level Since 2023
partialText: Officials at the central bank have embraced the possibility of higher interest rates to get resurgent inflation under control.

title: The Google Insider Trading Case Hits Polymarket
partialText: Charges against a Google employee who bet on Polymarket have raised concerns that the issue may dent momentum in the fast-growing sector.

title: Temu Hit With Fine in E.U. Over Sales of Unsafe Goods
partialText: The Chinese e-commerce platform faces a penalty of more than $230 million for selling baby toys and other products the European Commission said could harm consumers.

title: Genetic Scores are Booming. But Will Anti-Discrimination Laws Cover Your DNA?
partialText: As predictive medicine advances, legal scholars warn that decades-old federal guidelines could set up a potential clash between your genes and your job.

title: These Drivers Found Cheap Gas
partialText: It’s in Valley Center, Calif., on tribal land. Customers relish every penny saved.

title: My $7,300 United Business Class Seat Was Broken, and I Got a Pittance
partialText: A woman splurged for a lie-flat seat, but it got jammed in the horizontal position for most of the 14-hour flight. How much should United compensate her?

title: Streaming TV Bundles Grow in Popularity
partialText: Companies and their customers are embracing bundled streaming packages — but for different reasons.

title: Australia Sues 3M for $1.4 Billion Over ‘Forever Chemicals’
partialText: The lawsuit, the largest ever filed by the Australian government, claims 3M hid information about the harmful effects of PFAS used at military bases.

title: Oil Prices Ease on Possible Agreement for Strait’s Reopening
partialText: Oil prices jumped after the U.S. said it shot down four Iranian attack drones, casting doubt once again on the prospects for a peace deal.

title: What Plunging Pork Prices Say About China’s Economy
partialText: A key measure of inflation in China, they hit a 16-year low, driven by anemic consumer spending and an oversupply of hogs.

title: Court Orders Customs Chief to Address Compliance on Refunding Tariffs
partialText: The surprising demand to appear at a hearing suggested new concern about the Trump administration’s efforts to repay the full $166 billion owed from illegally imposed tariffs.

title: Condé Nast Pays Over $400,000 to 3 Journalists Fired Over Protest
partialText: The former workers were among a group of employees who confronted the company’s head of human resources about layoffs last fall.

title: KFF’s Chief Executive to Retire
partialText: Drew Altman, who transformed KFF from a little-known family foundation to a major source of U.S. health policy research, will step down at the end of the year.

title: ’60 Minutes’ Journalist Sharyn Alfonsi Loses Deal After Dispute With Bari Weiss
partialText: Sharyn Alfonsi, whose segment on a brutal Salvadoran prison was pulled abruptly in December, said that CBS News and its top editor, Bari Weiss, had let her contract expire.

title: Ferrari’s First Electric Car Runs Into Backlash in Italy and Beyond
partialText: Memes mocked the new model, analysts questioned its appeal and investors sold the automaker’s stock. A former Ferrari chairman warned of “the destruction of a legend.”

title: Global Supply Shortages Deepen as War Drags On, Risking Jobs and Growth
partialText: After three months, the fallout of the closure of the Strait of Hormuz is spreading, with developing countries bearing the brunt of the shortfall.

title: BP’s Former Chairman, Albert Manifold, Disputes How Company Characterized His Dismissal
partialText: Albert Manifold, who was abruptly fired less than a year after he was appointed, said he was let go “without explanation.”

title: Teachers Union Urges Schools to Curb A.I. Chatbots and Screen Time
partialText: The American Federation of Teachers recommended “no screens” at all for those in second grade or younger, and no A.I. chatbots for students in elementary school.
